# 1. Purpose

This document describes the architecture MarketMind is building toward if evidence earns it. It is not a claim that the adaptive allocator is already validated.

The current architecture target is a breadth-first layered system:

```text
Data panel
  -> governed input surface map
  -> signal family map
  -> child policies
  -> model / target / decision-rule matrix
  -> controlled narrowing
  -> survivor portfolio expression
  -> later-stage adaptation only if earned
```

The near-term research question is no longer whether a narrow W4-B router variant can be patched. It is whether a broad Phase II matrix can find candidates that survive controlled narrowing and then portfolio expression.

# 2. Current architecture reality

## 2.1 Data layer

The serious research panel is the adjusted Polygon/Massive US Stocks SIP daily panel. Raw OHLCV is preserved for price and liquidity filters; adjusted OHLCV is used for returns and labels; split and dividend adjustment factors are preserved; corporate-action and extreme-return diagnostics are available. Surface B was repaired after the corporate-action flag semantic fix.

## 2.2 Signal layer

Signals are weak transformations over the adjusted panel. Signal families include momentum, mean reversion, volatility, trend strength, drawdown, range compression, and volume proxy. W3-B added pandas-ta indicators with robust train-and-validation-only scaling and a KEEP / INVERT / DROP classification.

## 2.3 Child-policy layer

Current child policies include static, rolling IC, regime gate, XGBoost variants, simple ensemble, pandas-ta children, and cash. W3-B improved the child-policy layer on the clean primary surface but the result was concentrated and failed on the liquidity surface.

## 2.4 Router layer (current, weak baseline)

The current router is a recent-winner child-policy selector. It picks among child policies based on prior or recent child-policy performance. It is a weak baseline and is treated as such across all docs. It did not earn independent validation in W3.

Required terminology:

```text
Use:
  recent-winner router
  recent-winner child-policy selector
  weak baseline router

Avoid:
  learned meta-router
  adaptive meta-router
  meta-learning router
  true gating model
  Reptile router
  ML router
```

## 2.5 Broad matrix layer

The matrix layer evaluates model families, router targets, decision rules, and input surfaces before any survivor reaches portfolio expression.

Model families include Ridge, Elastic Net, Bayesian Ridge, Bayesian LASSO or sparse Bayesian proxy, Group LASSO, Sparse Group LASSO, PCR / PLS, XGBoost, Random Forest / ExtraTrees, quantile regression, contextual bandit, and mixture-of-experts. MAML / Reptile-style adaptation is later-stage only.

Router targets include child utility regression, child utility distribution, pairwise child-vs-best-child advantage, override probability, abstain probability, and regime classifier plus policy map.

Decision rules include free routing, default-to-best-child override, confidence-bound override, Thompson-style sampling, risk-adjusted expected utility, and drawdown-aware selection.

Input surfaces include TA child features, regime / liquidity / volatility, cross-asset, macro, sentiment / news, crypto-specific, and alternative data. Any missing PIT-safe source must be represented as blocked.

## 2.6 Portfolio layer

Portfolio expression is conditional on controlled narrowing. It covers position sizing, exposure caps, turnover caps, liquidity and capacity caps, transaction cost and slippage modelling, volatility targeting, drawdown overlays, cash / abstention, and rebalance cadence.

Liquidity treatment belongs here for survivor expression. W3-C demonstrated that liquidity score-time penalties at child level damage clean-surface results without recovering tradability.

## 2.7 Meta-learning and adaptation layer

Meta-learning and learned adaptation are optional and downstream. They become reasonable only when simpler families leave residual opportunity after P2-NARROW and at least one candidate is ready for portfolio expression.

# 3. Runtime target if earned

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A[Adjusted Polygon/Massive panel] --> B[Weak signal library + pandas-ta]
    A --> X[Blocked PIT-safe future inputs: macro, news, crypto, alt data]
    B --> C[Signal diagnostics and child policies]
    X --> M[Input surface map]
    C --> M
    M --> N[Model / target / decision-rule matrix]
    N --> O[Controlled narrowing]
    O --> P[Survivor portfolio expression]
    P --> R[Later-stage adaptation if earned]
```

The matrix and narrowing layers are research artifacts before they are runtime services. They do not imply production routing.

# 4. W3 outcomes and architectural implications

## 4.1 What W3 showed

The W3 lanes closed with real but fragile child-policy signal. The repaired clean primary surface anchored a strong best standalone child. The recent-winner router did not beat it. pandas-ta improved the child-policy layer but produced a concentrated result that failed on the liquidity surface. Liquidity treatment at child level damaged the clean surface without recovering the liquidity surface. The mechanism audit stopped inconclusive due to a replay-validation failure on row-level reconstruction.

Specific utilities, deltas, retention values, and replay failures are recorded in the Resolution Ledger.

## 4.2 What this means for architecture

1. The router layer is not the right place to add complexity. The recent-winner heuristic remains a weak baseline.
2. The broad candidate matrix and controlled narrowing layer are the next architectural surfaces to build; the portfolio layer follows only for survivors.
3. Liquidity treatment belongs in the portfolio layer, not in child-level score shaping.
4. Row-level decisions must be emitted at run time. Post-hoc reconstruction lost the mechanism audit; this is now a contract requirement.
5. Learned routing remains an architectural option, but only as part of the broad matrix and subsequent survivor evidence.

# 5. Required architecture changes for the broad reset

## 5.1 Architecture map and registries

The docs and artifact contract need explicit `architecture_map`, `model_family_registry`, `signal_family_registry`, and `surface_market_registry` surfaces. These identify available, blocked, and deferred inputs before modelling begins.

## 5.2 Candidate matrix and narrowing reports

The research harness needs a `candidate_matrix` and `narrowing_report` that record the model family, target, decision rule, input surface, comparator set, validation results, and narrowing classification.

## 5.3 Row-level decision emission

Every attribution-eligible run must emit immutable row-level selected decisions at run time per the Artifact Contract. Aggregation must reproduce report-level utilities before any classification or attribution is recorded.

## 5.4 Survivor portfolio harness

Only candidates classified `SURVIVOR_READY_FOR_PORTFOLIO` enter portfolio expression. The portfolio harness must compute sizing, cost, turnover, liquidity/capacity, concentration, drawdown, stress-window, and comparator metrics.

# 6. Conditional follow-up

## 6.1 If P2-NARROW produces survivors

Run P2-PORTFOLIO and classify each survivor using the existing W4 portfolio outcome labels. Later-stage adaptation can be proposed only if the survivor evidence shows residual opportunity that simpler families do not capture.

## 6.2 If P2-NARROW produces no survivors

Stop the run as a controlled narrowing result. Do not patch a single router variant to rescue the lane.

# 7. Explicit non-claims

This document does not claim:

- MarketMind has a validated adaptive allocator;
- the current router is a learned meta-router; it is a recent-winner selector;
- Reptile is the allocation brain;
- XGBoost is the winner;
- pandas-ta produced tradable alpha; it produced child-policy signal with concentration and liquidity-surface failure;
- the W3-D descriptive concentration share is the official Surface D classification;
- the project is execution-ready;
- production governance matters more than research truth.

The current architecture objective is:

```text
Build the broad Phase II architecture map and candidate matrix, narrow under predeclared controls, and express only survivors as portfolios.
```
